doc.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: His father's instrument business and visiting Havana musicians
summary: His father sold saxophones, clarinets and music from a small office, where Cachao, Chocolate Armenteros and Mario Bauza came by; his mother was a seamstress.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So your father in addition to learning to play the instrument, he actually sold the instruments as well.

He used to be the agent, very small agent in Havana, or the seller of saxophones. Sell many saxophones and clarinets also, and trumpets. He used to sell also accessories and printed music and things like that. So, that’s why I ran into people like Cachao; he used to go in there to buy his things and Chico’s father used to go there to buy trumpets, and Chocolate Armenteros, a family musicians for example, Mario Bauza was a dear friend of my father’s.
So all these gentlemen were coming around the house?
Yes; around this little office in the center of Havana.
Your father had an office in Havana?
He had a little office. In the center of Havana, just one room and a bathroom. Then he’d have all those instruments. I’d be in the toy store, because I used to go with him all the time.
My mother was a seamstress. She liked dress designing and everything like that. She retired against her will, when she was—I don’t know—almost 80 years old. She’s complaining.
